You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook vs. Seller counsel package dated as at 22 September 2026 data-room cut-off

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be disregarded

Before the substantive review, one procedural issue. The Seller's cover note states that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny" and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package".

**That is not correct and should not be acted on.**

- Nothing in our playbook records any agreement on these points. On the contrary, almost every [STANDARD] clause sits *directly opposite* our stated position (cap, thresholds, time limits, buyer knowledge, disclosure, Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay).
- The [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labelling is the Seller's own categorisation of its own draft. It has no contractual or negotiating status, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) says "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included".
- The Seller has marked *nothing* as [OPEN]. If we took the note at face value we would review nothing. That is the point of the note.

**Recommendation:** Treat every clause as open. Respond to Seller counsel in writing confirming that no clause has been "cleared" by Wattlebridge, that the limitation and disclosure packages are not agreed, and that the mark-up will address the full draft. We should also ensure no internal reviewer skips [STANDARD] items on the strength of this note.

---

## 1. Liability architecture (Clauses 12.1, 12.2, 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5, Fundamental/Title)

This is the most significant block of departures and the Seller's proposals are mutually reinforcing: a low cap, high thresholds, short tail, and then a sweep-up clause that drags *every* category of claim (title, tax, IP, indemnities, fraud) under that same regime.

### 1.1 General cap – Clause 12.1
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | **25% / AUD 6,000,000** (opening) |

The Seller has drafted straight to our *fallback* figure. The 20% position is usable **only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given**. We must not accept it and must not signal that it is acceptable.

**Push back:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not trade this early – the Seller's other asks (thresholds, time limit, categories) are far more aggressive and should be resolved first so the cap is not conceded in isolation.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | **AUD 5,000** |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | **AUD 50,000** |
| Recovery once basket exceeded | Excess only ("deductible") | **First dollar ("tipping")** |

Seller figures are 5x ours on both thresholds, and the switch from tipping to deductible means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is simply unrecoverable. Combined with a AUD 25,000 de minimis, on a AUD 24m deal this materially hollows out the warranty package for the kind of mid-size operational claims (e.g. supplier, employee, data issues) most likely to arise.

**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first dollar. This is a core economic term, not administrative.

### 1.3 Time limits – Clause 12.3 / 13
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General claims | 18 months | **24 months** |

18 months is our fallback and requires Amelia Frost's written approval; none given. 24 months also better matches a full post-Completion audit cycle plus investigation time.

**Push back:** 24 months.

### 1.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – Clause 13
This sentence is a hidden general-regime override and is contrary to the playbook's requirement to **keep Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant categories separate**. As drafted it would subject the Ironquay indemnity, any tax covenant, leakage/debt-free-cash-free adjustments and the fundamental warranties to the 20% cap, the AUD 250k deductible and the 18-month cut-off.

**Push back:** Delete. Replace with a clause stating that the general limitations apply *only* to General Warranty Claims and that each other category (Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants) is governed by its own regime.

### 1.5 Fundamental / Title warranties
Seller proposes capacity and title warranties "be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity".

This is unacceptable. If title to the shares fails, our loss is up to the full price; a 20% cap and 18-month tail would leave us exposed for AUD 19.2m+ with no recourse.

**Push back (playbook):** Separate regime – **100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any buyer-knowledge bar.**

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
"Of any nature" would, on its face, extend caps, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to claims for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. There is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller's package.

**Push back:** Insert an express carve-out: **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.** The playbook states no one on our side may waive this. Also narrow 9.3/12.8/20.5 to General Warranty Claims per 1.4.

---

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge (Schedule 7, Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2, Clause 8.3)

### 2.1 Deemed general disclosure
Disclosure Letter [1.1] discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room ... including DD-002 to DD-012"; [1.2] adds the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".

This is exactly the whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure the playbook rejects. Its practical effect: any warranty breach that can be reconstructed from *anything* in the data room (or from an ASIC/PPSR search we might have run) is deemed disclosed and un-claimable, regardless of whether the issue was flagged fairly.

**Push back:** Replace with a **specific fair disclosure** standard – disclosure is effective only to the extent the matter is fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter (and listed specific documents) with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete the data-room sweep and public-register deemed disclosure.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge exclusion – Clause 8.3
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

Three problems: (a) it is a blanket exclusion; (b) "discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – we don't even have to have actually known; (c) it extends to advisers, so a line in a DD report nobody acted on bars the claim. Read with 1.1/1.2 above and the all-Claims override in Clause 13, this would bar title and fraud claims too.

**Push back:** Delete Clause 8.3. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must (i) be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, (ii) be matched by Seller warranties qualified only by the actual knowledge of **named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry**, and (iii) **never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.**

### 2.3 Disclosure Letter [1.4] (non-admission)
Standard in form, but note it means the Seller is not conceding that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonus on-costs, DD-006 notification or Mossvale/lease consents are "required". That is fine as a non-admission, but it reinforces that we need these as express conditions/covenants rather than relying on disclosure.

---

## 3. Deal-specific matters

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3
- **Facts:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue). Change-of-control consent at clause 11.2 with conditions at 11.3. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**
- **Seller position:** "reasonable endeavours", consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- **Problem:** A customer that is 30% of revenue is a material customer. Reasonable endeavours is a weak obligation and does not deliver the consent; and "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent ignores that Bluefen's consent is *conditional* – a conditional consent delivered without the conditions met gives us nothing.

**Push back (playbook):** Condition precedent requiring (i) **effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent** from Bluefen under cl. 11.2, and (ii) **evidence that all cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion**. Seller obligation should be "all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours" with specific steps, and the Buyer should have a walk right if not satisfied by the long-stop date.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7
- **Facts:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control at 8.1; discharge at 9.2. Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms **not repaid, no discharge of security in the data room.**
- **Seller position:** release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Problem:** Deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-completion release means we would own a company with AUD 3.2m of bank debt, a change-of-control default risk under cl. 8.1, and security still registered over the assets. Leaving the discharge to the Seller's good faith after it has been paid is the worst position.

**Push back (playbook):** Require (i) a **current payout letter** from Riverlark in agreed form, (ii) **direct repayment from the Completion funds** flow to Riverlark, and (iii) **effective releases/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion**. A post-Completion release is acceptable only against an **irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark** and with **Amelia Frost's approval** – neither is in place, so the current draft is not acceptable.

### 3.3 Employee Completion bonuses (DD-005) – funds flow
- **Facts:** AUD 420,000 conditional on Completion and continued employment. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms the amounts are **not in the draft funds flow** and the Seller has **not addressed payroll tax, super or on-costs**.
- **Seller position:** "a matter for the Seller and ... not separately itemised".
- **Problem:** If they are "a matter for the Seller" they must be paid by the Seller or deducted from price; but if they are simply left out of the funds flow, the Company (i.e. us) pays them post-Completion. Being Completion-triggered, they are a transaction cost that falls squarely within the debt-free/cash-free principle. The on-cost point (payroll tax, SG, potentially ~10–15%+ on top) is unquantified.

**Push back (playbook):** AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must appear as a **specific line item** in the funds flow, either paid by the Seller or deducted from the price (and expressly treated as Debt/Transaction Expense in the price adjustment). Require Seller to quantify on-costs. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
- **Facts:** DD-004 cl. 7.3 – SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; Disclosure Letter para 4 says this is **not independent bank verification** and **no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room**.
- **Seller position:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Problem:** The exposure is not just the AUD 180k. If the fee is unpaid, title to the SOW3 Project Materials has not passed – that is an IP ownership gap in a company called "Analytics". The indemnity should cover loss from any failure of IP to vest, not just the cash fee. Note: the playbook is clear the AUD 180k figure is **not independently verified in either direction** – we should not assume it is unpaid, nor that it is paid.

**Push back (playbook):** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 Project Materials (and any other Ironquay deliverables), including costs of obtaining assignment, re-procurement and third-party claims; **preserve the SOW3 cure** (Seller to procure payment and a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion as the preferred route); keep this indemnity outside the general cap/basket/time limit (see 1.4). Ask Seller for bank evidence of payment status.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006) – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6
- **Facts:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Investigation preliminary; **no finding either way on access, scope or notification obligation**; no loss amount.
- **Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter ... not expected to be material".
- **Assessment:** The playbook position is deliberately neutral – assume **no confirmed breach, no harm, no notification duty and no numeric demand in either direction**. We should not accept "not material" as a disclosed conclusion, but nor should we assert a breach. What we need is process.

**Push back (playbook):** Covenants requiring the Seller/Company to (i) **preserve all logs and evidence**, (ii) **complete the investigation** (access logs for the link, whether downloaded, scope), (iii) **provide updates to the Buyer** through to Completion, and (iv) take any notification step a reasonable investigation concludes is required. Add a specific warranty that the Disclosure Letter description is complete; consider a specific indemnity for loss from this incident, outside the general regime, with no numeric assumption. The "not expected to be material" language should not be treated as a disclosure against any privacy/data warranty.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Facts:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000). Disclosure Letter para 8 says the Seller does **not** state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – yet the Update calls them "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Assessment:** The two Seller documents are internally inconsistent. The playbook says **assess – no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.**

**Push back:** Request the three renewal documents read together (timing/scope per the Letter), termination rights, whether any amount is accrued at Completion, and whether the renewals were committed in the ordinary course. Reserve position on classification pending that information; do not accept the "ordinary course" label as a disclosure or as a conclusion.

### 3.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Lease: notification obligation only; not stated as a landlord consent requirement. Mossvale: restriction on assignment; share sale not stated to trigger consent.
- These are not framed as departures, but the Disclosure Letter's careful phrasing ("does not state ... required") leaves open the possibility. **Action:** confirm by reviewing the underlying clauses ourselves; require a Seller covenant to give the DD-007 notification before Completion; obtain a warranty that no counterparty consent is triggered by the share sale under either agreement.

### 3.8 Tax / IP
Seller: "settled under the general regime above". Playbook: **Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; no unlimited liability; no resolution assumed.**

**Push back:** Reject the characterisation. Tax and IP warranties and any tax covenant/indemnity are to be negotiated separately, with their own cap and time limits (playbook does not call for unlimited liability). They must sit outside Clause 13's general override.

### 3.9 Title
Seller: title evidenced by the share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this identifies "the source relied on" and does **not** state the Buyer has completed its own verification.

**Push back (playbook):** The DD-012 register is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof**. Require: current ASIC company extract and member list; PPSR search over the shares/Seller; copies of share certificates; Seller board/shareholder resolutions and constitution authority evidence; a warranty of no encumbrance over the shares; and a Riverlark-specific confirmation that no security over the shares exists or is released at Completion. Fundamental warranties on title and capacity on the separate regime per 1.5.

---

## 4. Summary table

| # | Item | Seller draft | Playbook | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "Efficiency Note" | [STANDARD] = cleared, skip review | Not agreed; review everything | **Reject outright** |
| 1.1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | 25% / 6.0m (fallback needs Frost authority – none) | High |
| 1.2 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k, deductible | 5k / 50k, first dollar | High |
| 1.3 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months (fallback needs Frost authority – none) | High |
| 1.4 | Cl. 13 all-Claims override | Limits apply to all Claims | Separate categories | **Critical** |
| 1.5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | 100%, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/knowledge | **Critical** |
| 1.6 | Fraud carve-out | None; limits apply "of any nature" | Full carve-out, non-waivable | **Critical** |
| 2.1 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure | High |
| 2.2 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable", advisers | Delete; narrow qualifier only | High |
| 3.1 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | Effective consent + conditions evidenced pre-Completion | **Critical** (30% revenue) |
| 3.2 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion | **Critical** (AUD 3.2m) |
| 3.3 | Bonuses DD-005 | Not itemised | Line item + on-costs, Seller-funded | High |
| 3.4 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 payment indemnity | Broad IP-vesting indemnity, preserve cure | High |
| 3.5 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preserve/investigate/update; no assumption | Medium |
| 3.6 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Assess; no automatic treatment | Medium |
| 3.8 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | Open; separate regime | High |
| 3.9 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence | High |

---

## 5. Recommendations

1. **Respond on the Efficiency Note first.** Short letter to Seller counsel: nothing is agreed, [STANDARD] has no status, full mark-up to follow. Do not let the labelling frame the negotiation.
2. **Lead with the structural points, not the numbers.** Clause 13's all-Claims override, the absence of a fraud carve-out, and the collapsing of Fundamental/Title into the general regime are the items that would most damage us even if we won every number. Fix the architecture (separate categories; fraud carved out; Fundamental at 100%/6 years), then negotiate the general cap/thresholds/tail.
3. **Hold the playbook numbers.** 25% / AUD 6m; AUD 5k / 50k first-dollar; 24 months. The Seller has opened at our fallbacks – do not confirm them. Any movement to 20% or 18 months requires Amelia Frost's **prior written** authority identifying the draft; obtain it before, not after, any concession.
4. **Rewrite the disclosure/knowledge package.** Specific fair disclosure only; delete the data-room and public-register sweep; delete Clause 8.3 or replace with a narrow actual-knowledge/named-persons/reasonable-enquiry qualifier that never touches title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
5. **Make Bluefen and Riverlark hard Completion deliverables.** Bluefen: effective consent with cl. 11.3 conditions evidenced, as a CP. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion. Neither is currently in place per the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, so both are gating items for timetable.
6. **Fix the funds flow.** Add the DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a Seller-borne line item. Ask Seller to confirm super/payroll tax treatment.
7. **Broaden Ironquay; keep the cure.** Indemnity for IP-vesting failure, outside the general regime; Seller to procure payment confirmation and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion. Obtain bank evidence on the AUD 180k.
8. **DD-006: process covenants, no conclusions.** Log preservation, completion of investigation, updates to us, notification if required; specific indemnity with no assumed quantum.
9. **Sandbar: information request, reserve position.** Do not accept "ordinary course" or treat as Debt until the renewals are assessed.
10. **Title: commission independent verification** (ASIC extract, PPSR, certificates, authority documents) rather than relying on DD-012.
11. **Tax and IP remain open** and should be carved out of any "settled" language in the Seller's next turn.

I can prepare the mark-up of Clauses 2, 3, 6.3, 7, 8.3, 9.3, 11.1, 12, 13 and 20.5 and a draft response to Seller counsel on the Efficiency Note if that would be useful.
=== END ADVICE ===
